He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles]], [[Arkansas Tech Wonder Boys]] and [[Liberty Flames basketball|Liberty Flames]]. He was selected by the Pacers in the second round of the [[2025 NBA draft]]. ==Early life and high school career== Peter was born on February 27, 2002, and grew up in [[Russellville, Arkansas]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.ttusports.com/sports/mbkb/2020-21/bios/peter_taelon_t8na|publisher=[[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles]]|title=Taelon Peter}} He attended [[Russellville High School (Arkansas)|Russellville High School]] where he competed in [[basketball]] and [[track and field]] as a [[high jump]]er.{{Cite web|url=https://www.rivervalleynow.com/local_sports/the-state-record-that-never-was/article_c65a8440-c225-11ea-a577-1f43bfbcdfb5.html|website=RiverValleyNow.com|title=The state record that never was|date=July 9, 2020|last=May|first=Easton}} He won two state championships in the high jump and in basketball, averaged 16 points per game as a [[Senior (education)|senior]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.wholehogsports.com/news/2020/jan/16/russellvilles-taelon-peter-just-starting-heat/|website=WholeHogSports.com|title=Russellville's Taelon Peter just starting to heat up |date=January 16, 2020|last=Davenport|first=Richard}} He was all-state in track and field and was named the Class 5A West Player of the Year, River Valley Now Player of the Year, all-state and all-conference in basketball. After high school, he signed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles men's basketball|Tennessee Tech]] in 2020.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-and-advance/175377115/|newspaper=[[The News & Advance]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=January 24, 2025|page=B1, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-and-advance/175377181/ B4]|title=Peter excels as 6th man|last=Gordon|first=Bryson}} {{Open access}} ==College career== Peter only played six games as a [[freshman]] for Tennessee Tech in 2020–21 before transferring to the [[NCAA Division II]]-level [[Arkansas Tech Wonder Boys]]. He averaged 10 points playing in 25 games off the bench for Arkansas Tech in 2021–22. He then became a starter in 2022–23, averaging 15.5 points while shooting 44% from the field. In 2023–24, he was named the [[Great American Conference]] (GAC) Player of the Year and first-team All-GAC after averaging 18.5 points and starting every game for the Wonder Boys.{{Cite news|url=https://www.magnoliareporter.com/sports/southern_arkansas_sports/article_f7cc5d16-dc6e-11ee-b197-7b09ababe016.html|newspaper=[[Magnolia Reporter]]|title=Taelon Peter of ATU top men's player in GAC |date=March 7, 2024}} Peter finished his three-year stint at Arkansas Tech with overall averages of 15 points and 5.2 rebounds and transferred to the [[Liberty Flames basketball|Liberty Flames]] for his final year of eligibility in 2024–25.{{Cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/06/26/who-is-indiana-pacers-nba-draft-pick-taelon-peter-out-of-liberty-2025-no-54-second-round/84332875007/|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|title=Who is Pacers' pick Taelon Peter? 'This is why the NBA draft is beautiful because you hear guys like Taelon Peter hearing their name'|last=Glenesk|date=June 26, 2025|first=Matthew}} In one season with the Flames, he averaged 13.7 points and four rebounds, being selected third-team All-[[Conference USA]] and the Conference USA Sixth Man of the Year.{{Cite news|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2025/06/26/nba-draft-2025-indiana-pacers-take-liberty-shooter-taelon-peter-with-no-54-pick-second-round/84380061007/|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|title=Pacers take Liberty sharpshooter Taelon Peter with the No. 54 pick in NBA draft|last=Dopirak|date=June 26, 2025|first=Dustin}} He led the conference in [[free throw]] percentage and also was the national leader with a true shooting percentage of 72.4%, "a statistic that combines field goal and free throw shooting proficiency". ==Professional career== Peter was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the second round (54th overall) of the [[2025 NBA draft]]. He made 38 appearances for Indiana during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 4.5 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 1.1 assists. On July 20, 2026, Peter was waived by the Pacers.{{Cite web|title=Taelon Peter: Let go by Pacers|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/taelon-peter-let-go-by-pacers/|access-date=August
